story.label: WHY I STARTED
story.heading: A little more connection, close to home.
story.lede: I imagined an overlooked patch of ground becoming a place where anyone could feel welcome.
paragraphs: That idea became Common Ground Project: a community garden concept built around growing fresh food and growing stronger neighborhood connections at the same time. I wanted the garden to be about more than what we harvest. It should also be a place to learn by doing, share skills, and get to know the people around you.

I believe getting involved should feel approachable. You don’t need gardening experience or a perfect plan to begin; curiosity and a little willingness to pitch in are enough. My hope is to help create a project where neighbors shape the garden together and everyone has something to bring.

bio.label: A LITTLE MORE ABOUT ME
bio.heading: Student, creator,
bio.intro: I’m Lexis Bermudo, a 21-year-old BSIT student at Angeles University Foundation. I’m based in Mabalacat City, where I’m learning, building ideas, and finding ways to bring people together.

items.title: Start with neighbors
items.description: People who live nearby should shape the spaces and the decisions that affect them.

items.title: Make it welcoming
items.description: Gardens should be easy to join, generous with knowledge, and open to all experience levels.

items.title: Share what grows
items.description: Food, skills, time, and care all become more valuable when they move between people.
